data.current_summary: get_status for a task, with a message to the operator
data.current_description: This is get_status with the optional message, as a POST so that the text is in the body, not in the URL (which servers log). Without a message (empty body, or {"message": null}) it is a plain status call, like the GET. With a message it is written to the thread and e-mailed to the operator, and the answer is the same as the GET's, including your message (from: agent) and message_sent: true. Read the operator's message first, then reply: while the operator has written something you have not read yet, nothing is stored or e-mailed; the answer is the GET's, with that message in messages, message_sent: false and a next_action that says so, and you send your answer with the next call (HTTP 200 either way, so check message_sent). Plain text, 1-2000 characters, never interpreted as HTML; an empty or longer message is a 400. Limits: 10 messages per hour per quote (its quote_id and task_id share it) and 30 per hour per client address (429). The same text again within 10 minutes, while it is still the newest message of the thread, is not stored or e-mailed a second time (the answer then has duplicate_ignored: true). It needs the same access_token as the GET; without one, or with another quote's, nothing is stored or sent (401).
data.summary_suggestion: Get task status and send message to operator
data.description_suggestion: Retrieves the current task status and optionally sends a message to the operator. The message (1-2000 characters, plain text) is written to the operator thread and e-mailed if this is the first unread message from the agent. Without a message (empty body or {"message": null}), this performs a plain status check. Returns the complete task record with message_sent indicating whether the message was delivered. Rate limited: 10 messages per hour per quote, 30 per hour per client address. Duplicate messages within 10 minutes are ignored (duplicate_ignored: true). Requires valid access_token for the quote.

data.current_summary: Open a payment link: redirects to a Stripe Checkout page
data.current_description: The payment link that create_task (and get_status while a payment is due) returns as checkout_url; you do not build it yourself. It carries a signature and an expiry: 4 days from when the payment was created, 28 days for a balance. Opening it redirects (303) to the Stripe Checkout page of the payment: the page that is still open, or a fresh one if Stripe's own page (24 hours) has expired meanwhile. Nothing is created twice: a page that is still open is reused. After the link has expired it answers 410 with a short page; nothing is charged then and no contract is concluded (ask for a new quote). A test order has no payment link (409). Safe to open in a browser; not meant to be called by an agent, which should hand the link to the user or the operator.
data.summary_suggestion: Redirect to Stripe Checkout for task payment
data.description_suggestion: Redirects to the Stripe Checkout page for paying a task invoice. This endpoint is provided by create_task and get_status as checkout_url; do not construct it manually. The link is valid for 4 days (initial payment) or 28 days (balance payment) from creation. Returns a 303 redirect to Stripe's payment page. If the Stripe page has expired (24 hours), a fresh page is created. Expired links return 410 Gone. Test orders return 409 (no payment available). This endpoint is intended for users/operators to open in a browser, not for agents to call directly.

data.current_summary: Send a task to a human for screening and a fixed-price quote
data.current_description: Not binding. A human answers within 24 hours (every day, including weekends and Czech public holidays). Required: description, email and name (the name of the person or company for the invoice); delivery_address is required too when a physical item is to be shipped, handed over or collected. The fields can be sent flat, at the top level (QuoteRequestFlat, the shape smaller models get right), or nested under task / client / agent (QuoteRequestNested); both are accepted, also mixed, and if a field is sent both ways the nested one wins. A missing required field is a 400 that names the field and shows an example. Put everything the user told you (quantity, material, colour, size, address) into the fields or into description. For name use the company or person from the shipping address (or the company the user gave); do not ask the user for it, ask only if there is neither. If the user gave an address, its country is the country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). A VAT id only if the user gave one: never guess or make one up. Never invent a quote_id or a status: a real quote_id starts with q_ and comes only from this tool's own response. The answer carries quote_id and access_token: Tell the user to save the access_token now: it is shown once and is the only key to the quote and the task. If the access_token is lost: POST https://api.handsforagents.com/v1/quotes/{quote_id}/access-token (REST only, not a tool); a new one is sent to the contact e-mail. get_status cannot recover it.
data.summary_suggestion: Submit a task request for human screening and quote
data.description_suggestion: Submits a task description to a human operator for screening and receives a non-binding fixed-price quote. The operator responds within 24 hours (daily, including weekends and Czech public holidays). Required fields: description, email, name (person or company for invoice), and delivery_address (if physical shipment/handover/collection is needed). Accepts both flat (QuoteRequestFlat) and nested (QuoteRequestNested) field formats; nested values take precedence if duplicated. Returns quote_id (starts with q_) and access_token (shown once only—critical for all subsequent operations). The access_token can be recovered via POST /quotes/{quote_id}/access-token if lost. No authentication required for this operation.

data.current_description: Always read next_action: one or two sentences on what to do now (wait; review the quote and call create_task; pay checkout_url; call confirm_delivery), with paid, quote_valid_until and expected_ship_date. messages is the thread with the operator, newest first (from: operator or agent). Every status can change at any time: call again whenever the user asks, never answer from memory, and report only what the response says, without conclusions of your own. This REST answer is always the complete record; the MCP tools get_status, create_task and confirm_delivery answer briefly by default (get_status with full=true returns this complete record). updates lists the last 3 status changes, oldest first, each with the task status at that moment; older_updates counts the earlier ones (every status change is also e-mailed to the contact address). To answer an operator question, call get_status with message: send the same request as POST with a JSON body {"message": "..."} (plain text, 1-2000 characters); it is stored in the same thread and e-mailed to the operator, and the answer is the usual status, including your message (message_sent: true). Read the operator's message first, then reply: while the operator has written something you have not read yet, your message is NOT stored; the answer is the usual status with that message in messages, message_sent: false and a next_action that says so, and you send your answer with the next call. Send it once and only with what the user told you: the same text again within 10 minutes is ignored (duplicate_ignored: true). E-mail to tasks@handsforagents.com with the quote_id in the subject still works. test_mode true marks a test order: nothing is paid or invoiced.

Status can change at any time—always call again to get current state rather than relying on cached responses. Requires the access_token from the quote creation response.

data.current_description: Always read next_action: one or two sentences on what to do now (wait; review the quote and call create_task; pay checkout_url; call confirm_delivery), with paid, quote_valid_until and expected_ship_date. messages is the thread with the operator, newest first (from: operator or agent). Every status can change at any time: call again whenever the user asks, never answer from memory, and report only what the response says, without conclusions of your own. This REST answer is always the complete record; the MCP tools get_status, create_task and confirm_delivery answer briefly by default (get_status with full=true returns this complete record). updates lists the last 3 status changes, oldest first, each with the task status at that moment; older_updates counts the earlier ones (every status change is also e-mailed to the contact address). To answer an operator question, call get_status with message: send the same request as POST with a JSON body {"message": "..."} (plain text, 1-2000 characters); it is stored in the same thread and e-mailed to the operator, and the answer is the usual status, including your message (message_sent: true). Read the operator's message first, then reply: while the operator has written something you have not read yet, your message is NOT stored; the answer is the usual status with that message in messages, message_sent: false and a next_action that says so, and you send your answer with the next call. Send it once and only with what the user told you: the same text again within 10 minutes is ignored (duplicate_ignored: true). E-mail to tasks@handsforagents.com with the quote_id in the subject still works. test_mode true marks a test order: nothing is paid or invoiced.
